records.content:
As a new semester begins

Lord Protector

Heavenly Father

Perfect Glorious Creator

How Amazing are Your Deeds

We Delight in All of Your Works

All You do is Just and Good

Please give us the sight to see all of Your Good and Wonderful Works

Let us see Your Beauty revealed in,

the Chemistry of Your creation to explore,

the Code which we create programs for Your Glory,

the Physics of motion that You gave Your Creation to explore,

the Literature written by Creation for Your Glory,

and all things You have put before us to study for Your Glory,

As we delight in you to ponder your great works.

Please grant us the sight to see your Work in all of these things,

Let us see your beauty in

Our struggles with a difficult course,

Our laughter after a good lab,

Our Tears after a difficult assignment,

Our Anxiety for a test,

Our Joy in a group assignment,

Our Exaustion from a long night,

As we delight in Glorifying you through our Endurance.

For all of these things were Your Will, Lord,

As we may throw the dice, you will determine how they fall Lord.

For not a hair may fall from our heads without the will of our Father in Heaven.

For we know, that we belong to our Saviour Jesus Christ,

And that all things through our lives will be at the Lords will,

And that we belong to him, Christ, by his Holy Spirt,

And are living our lives for the Glory of the Lord.

Loving God, help us to endure through this coming semester for your Glory,

So that we may delight and explore your creation,

So that we may serve You, The King of Kings, and ruler of our lives,

And Glorify you in every way.

Lead us towards your Love, and your Wisdom as we embark on this semester,

May we reflect your Love in our work, and your Delight in Creation,

And do all things in your Glory.

Amen.

records.content:
For preparing or revising a course

Heavenly Father, you prepared a wonderful course of instruction for me, as I grew from an embryo to an adult through the nurture and admonition of my parents, and teachers and my daily exploration of your deeply rich world.

Now I get to form and nurture a learning community in a much smaller and shorter scale. But I expect it will still be a rich experience for everyone, because your image-bearers are coming together to learn about your world.

Anchor my vision and plans in what is true, humble, just, pure, commendable, praiseworthy.

Help me start and continue with Jesus, because He is the true purpose of it all.

So form my objectives to align with what you desire—not just knowledge/skills, but how you’ll work through us to live together... how you’ll grow all of us.

Guide my design of assessments that will serve us to align our efforts with good objectives. Protect me from both laziness and overeagerness and perfectionism. Guide me to leave room for your Spirit’s work in all of us.

As I plan, give me a deep appreciation for what you have done in past offerings of this and similar courses, so I can build on what is good.

Give me humility to temper my aspirations, where I hold my future self and my students to unrealistic expectations.

Guard me from the frantic, fearful search for just the right materials, activities, structures, policies... help me trust you.

This is a long game. Help me focus & stay grounded.

And most importantly, send your Spirit in my classroom to teach what I never could.

Starting the day

Good morning, King of the Universe

As my body starts to realize it is a new day, I turn to you

As I sip from my cup and think about the day ahead, you remind me that you are always present

I praise you for a night of rest and restoration

And for the tasks that await  me at my computer

I thank you for the great duty of finding order in the code I create

As you created me in your image, I am also able to create

As Adam and Eve rebelled against you, I am also able to destroy

Create for good, create for evil

Destroy for good, destroy for evil

In this morning’s glimpse of a new day, I turn to you

As I smell my coffee, and think about the challenges ahead of me, you remind me to be holy as you are

You invite me to use my hands to bring into existence programs that glorify you

To gift the world with code that proclaims your glory

May my code be creative, effective, hospitable

May my code prevent others of making mistakes, and keep me from dragging myself into sloppy solutions

May my code be a reflection of the love I have for you and for my neighbor

If I need to delete parts of my code, may I be wise enough to avoid wasting time coding things that won’t work, as a good steward should

If I forget specifics and leave some functions behind, may I remember that you never forget us

Enlighten me when I get stuck, not knowing what to do next

And join me in joy when my code runs smoothly

May my code be a reflection of who you want me to be

And as I finish my morning coffee and turn to the important work I need to do

Let not me be distracted by other things

Make my heart rest, knowing you will take care of my beloved ones and my coworkers

So I don’t need to constantly check my messages and emails

Make my mind focused and disposed to find satisfaction in the coding and nothing more

So I don’t get myself lost in the infinite timelines of social media and sensationalist news

Help me today, Lord

I will open my computer, and I will worship you with all I am

A creature whose core is programmed to love you through my programs

Amen.

For when one of my professors retire

Through this journey of life Lord,

I have seen you near and far,

For everything in this world is Yours.

I know you have plans for all of us,

And this plan you are enacting will bring joy to many,

I thank you for the Joy that they have brought in their time here.

Give them strength as you send them from this place,

Give them strength in their new callings,

Give them the strength to rest after many years of work for your Glory,

For you are great, and you have given us the command to live by:

Love your neighbor as ourselves,

We so have loved having them in our place of study.

And they so lived in love throughout their time here,

I thank you Father,

for the oppertunity to get to love and meet them,

To be mentored by them,

To laugh with them,

To have a chance to talk seriously with them about what matters to us,

We thank you for the oppertunities you have given them,

That they may show how amazing our your deeds, Lord,

And how we may delight in studying them.

We may have peace in knowing that,

Not a hair can fall from our heads,

Not a professor can retire,

Not a day can be had,

Without your will in heaven, Lord.

We pray in your great and holy name, Lord.

Understanding computational complexity

Heavenly Father

Infinite

Perfect

Unfathomable

Not a drop of Jesus blood was wasted

Not a single strand of hair falls without your consent

You eternal nature is mysterious

And your days are more than an O(n!) algorithm.

Our O(n) days provides us with a sense of continuity

And a false impression that they will tend to the infinite

But our days are counted

In your eyes, the number of our days are like an O(1) algorithm

Short. Fast. Fleeting.

Teach us how to count our days as we wrestle counting the operations in our algorithms

As we seek to find an efficient solution to the problems we face in our discipline

Teach us that we are limited and Your creation has boundaries that should be respected

God of order, how to sort things out?

Serving the scholarly community

Lord of all, righteous judge who sees all as it truly is,

Today I face the reality of a commitment I made some time ago

to be servant critic of the work of some of your other children,

whose names and stories I may never know,

and who may never know my name.

Grant foremost that your name be known throughout this process—

that as we study the world you made we’d see the fingerprints of its Maker,

that as we communicate we would speak the truth in love even as we don’t know each other,

that whether my words be encouraging or critical that they would point their readers, somehow, to you.

Grant me the heart of a servant, working for your praise, not the praise of people.

Grant me insight and perception in this process,

not just for what is flawed, lacking, or suspicious,

but for what grace you have given to these researchers

as they have sought to understand your world.

Help me to see good in their work that they may not have seen themselves.

Grant me perseverance to follow through with this process to completion,

even when I’m unsure whether my understanding and perception are correct

or whether my words are accurate, constructive, or too harsh.

Use this quiet service to build our collective understanding,

to fan into flame the embers of promising ideas,

to purify and refine work that mixes gold and dross,

and to keep watch for what might seek to dilute truth.

Thank you that I’m not the ultimate judge of this work, yet alone the people who made it.

Jesus will come again to judge the living and the dead.`

And when I feel tired and discouraged by this work, remind me you’re here.

Glorious God

Perfect Lord

Creator of all that is Good

We ask for self control so that we do not let our walls be broken down,
broken down by the busyness in our lives,
broken down by our temptations to do wrong,
broken down by choosing not to do what is right even when we know what is right,
broken down by letting the world taking control of our lives.

For we know in life and death,
We are yours forever.

Yours in Eternal Love,
And by your Son, Jesus Christ,
Our Lord and Saviour.

Let us be reminded of the sacrifice of our Holy Lord, Jesus Christ,
So we may sacrifice the parts of our habits that do not Glorify you, Lord.

Let us sacrifice

Our Procrastination,
Choosing to not do what we ought to do,
even when we know what is right for your Glory,

Our Love for Human Satisfaction,
Choosing to befriend the world,
Making us an enemy of you, God.

Our selfish ambition,
Wanting to become the lords of our own lives.

For we know that you, Lord, are our Father in Heaven,
Our Protector, Who sent His Son, Christ Jesus, to die for our sin.

Let us Glorify you with our work, all of it that is Good, and for your Glory.

Let us Delight in sacrificing the busyness of this world, for you, God.

Keep our eyes fixed on your Wisdom, that above all knowledge in this world,
Your Wisdom that endures forever, and grants us Eternal Life.

For we must remember the King of Kings who we work for on this earth,
The Lord of our Lives, and the Protector of us.
We will not work for the obscure men of this world,
But for you, Lord.

We ask for your Divine Guidance and Wisdom to guide us in the tasks ahead,
Which tasks we need to sacrifice, so that we may Glorify you in all that we do.

We ask for Rest, from the constant motion of this world,
For you have shown us what is right, and we alone cannot uphold all things,
We put our faith in you Alone, Christ, God, and Holy Spirit.

Let the Holy Spirit guide us to doing what is right for you in our every action,
For our lives belong completely to you, Lord.

Welcome to a collection of prayers written for those who study, teach, and practice the craft of computing. I am Eric Araujo, professor of Computer Science at Calvin University and the curator of this collection. You are invited to explore, use, and contribute to these prayers as you seek to integrate your faith with your work in computer science.

In the discipline of Computer Science, we encounter profound questions about logic, creation, beauty, and human flourishing. These prayers are offered as a resource for students and professors who wish to integrate their faith with their intellectual work.

Whether you’re starting a new semester, debugging stubborn code, wrestling with imposter syndrome, or preparing to teach a difficult concept, these prayers invite you to bring your whole self—mind, heart, and soul—before God.

Explore our 

collection of Prayers, including:

A Prayer for the Beginning of a Semester - For professors and students as a new term begins

Grasping Big-O notation and complexity - For students wrestling with understanding algorithm complexity

Reviewing others’ papers - For the professor asked to review a colleague’s scholarly work
